# Public Modifier

#### Course: Learn C++ OOP

## Public Modifier

As the name suggests, variables and functions declared with the public access modifier can be accessed from any class. Let's see an example,

```cpp
1#include <iostream>
2using namespace std;
3
4class Student {
5    
6
7    // public variable
8    public:
9        string name;
10
11};
12
13int main() {
14    
15    // create object of Student
16    Student student1;
17    
18
19    // access the public variable of the Student class
20    student1.name = "Rosie";
21    cout << "Student Name: " << student1.name << endl;
22
23    
24    return 0;
25}
26
27// Output: Student Name: Rosie
```

In the above example, we have used the public access modifier with the name variable. That's why we are able to assign a new value and access its value from the main() function.

![The public variable inside a class can be accessed from outside](data:image/png;base64,)
